heroes_maternal_population.long_name: Total population of the area used in the ARPA-H HEROES Maternal Health severe obstetric complications snapshot
heroes_maternal_population.short_description: Total population of the geography as reported alongside the SOC rate snapshot.
heroes_maternal_population.long_description: Total population denominator reported by the ARPA-H Outcome Toolkit for a given ZCTA3, state, or national area at the time of the Maternal Health export. Provided for context when interpreting the SOC rate, not as an independent outcome measure.

heroes_maternal_soc_rate_low.long_name: Lower bound of the binned rate of severe obstetric complications (SOC) per 10,000 deliveries
heroes_maternal_soc_rate_low.short_description: Lower bound of the SOC rate range bucket for this area.
heroes_maternal_soc_rate_low.long_description: The ARPA-H Outcome Toolkit reports the SOC rate (rate of severe obstetric complications during the delivery hospitalization and 60 days postpartum per 10,000 deliveries, open claims only) only as a map-legend bucket (e.g. "192.3 to 243.9"), never as a single point value. This is the numeric lower bound of that bucket. Use alongside heroes_maternal_soc_rate_high and heroes_maternal_soc_rate_label -- do not average low/high into a point estimate, since the true value's position within the bucket is unknown.
heroes_maternal_soc_rate_low.statement: In {location}, the SOC rate fell between {value} and {heroes_maternal_soc_rate_high} per 10,000 deliveries.

heroes_maternal_soc_rate_high.long_name: Upper bound of the binned rate of severe obstetric complications (SOC) per 10,000 deliveries
heroes_maternal_soc_rate_high.short_description: Upper bound of the SOC rate range bucket for this area.
heroes_maternal_soc_rate_high.long_description: Numeric upper bound of the same map-legend bucket described in heroes_maternal_soc_rate_low. See that field's description for the bucket-vs-point-estimate caveat.
heroes_maternal_soc_rate_high.statement: In {location}, the SOC rate fell between {heroes_maternal_soc_rate_low} and {value} per 10,000 deliveries.

heroes_maternal_soc_rate_label.long_name: Qualitative label for the severe obstetric complications (SOC) rate bucket, relative to the national average
heroes_maternal_soc_rate_label.short_description: Text label describing this area's SOC rate relative to the national average (e.g. "Slightly Lower than National Average").
heroes_maternal_soc_rate_label.long_description: The Outcome Toolkit's own qualitative classification of the SOC rate bucket, ranging from "Low Outlier" through "High Outlier", or "No Data" where the area had no reportable rate. Mirrors the map legend shown in the Toolkit UI.
heroes_maternal_soc_rate_label.statement: In {location}, the SOC rate was classified as "{value}".

heroes.name: ARPA-H Outcome Toolkit -- HEROES Program Area Snapshots
heroes.organization: ARPA-H (Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health)
heroes.location: Outcome Toolkit exports (Results_<Topic>_<date>_<AREA>.csv) for the HEROES program's target health challenges
heroes.description: The HEROES (Health care Rewards to Achieve Improved Outcomes) program is an ARPA-H initiative that pays 'Health Accelerators' for demonstrated, quantifiable reductions in one of four targeted health challenges: alcohol-related harms, cardiovascular disease and risk, opioid overdoses, and severe pregnancy/birth complications. ARPA-H's own 'Outcome Toolkit' web app lets accelerators pick candidate project geographies and track performance against a payment target. This repo ingests the Toolkit's exported area-level snapshots (CSV) for three of the four targets -- Maternal Health (severe obstetric complications), Heart Attack and Stroke Risk (ASCVD), and Opioid Overdose -- an Alcohol-Related Health Harms export does not exist yet. Per the Toolkit's own disclosure: 'Data on [these outcomes] are provided by HealthVerity from multiple sources and represent aggregate reports based upon open claims data, hospital charge data, and mortality data for the periods covered. It is important to note that the data displayed in the Outcome Toolkit are not intended to represent the entire US population.' Each outcome is only exposed as a binned map-legend range (never a raw point value), and Maternal/ASCVD use 3-digit ZCTA geography while Opioid uses real county FIPS. The Toolkit UI displays these as a six-month rolling average ending on a specific month (shown on-screen, e.g. 'Feb 2025'), but that reference month is not present in the CSV export itself -- only the export run date is recoverable, so treat `time` in standard/ as a placeholder, not a confirmed reporting period, until future exports capture the true rolling-window end date.
heroes.restrictions: Not publicly licensed/documented by ARPA-H at time of ingest; confirm redistribution terms before wider release.
